frozen_candidate_root_contribution: Forward displacement in time relative to a due term: bringing about, seeking, or embodying the arrival of something BEFORE its appointed/completed measure (the counter-pole of >jl 'appointed term' and t-A-x-r 'deferral').

internal_discovery.candidate_root_contribution: Forward displacement in time relative to a due term: bringing about, seeking, or embodying the arrival of something BEFORE its appointed/completed measure (the counter-pole of >jl 'appointed term' and t-A-x-r 'deferral').
internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Across all 47 occurrences the root marks not mere speed but prematurity — something pulled ahead of a set point of completion. Form X (19x + its verbal noun) is always "demanding God's threatened decree arrive before its term," and the verses themselves supply the term being violated (ajal musamman 29:53, ajaluhum 10:11, maw'id 18:58, qabla yawmi al-hisab 38:16, min qabli an yuqda ilayka wahyuhu 20:114). Form II is delivering a thing early (advance payment of this-life share 17:18, early portion of promised spoils 48:20). The base verb is acting ahead of a running count or an incomplete process (19:84, 20:84, 75:16). al-'ajilah is "the life that arrives first" opposed to the deferred heavy day (76:27). 'ajal (21:37) names the disposition itself, with explicit root wordplay. The calf ('ijl, 10x) reads as the pre-mature bovine, and the Quran itself welds the idol-calf to root-haste verbs: a'jalaka/'ajiltu (20:83-84) directly precede the calf of 20:88, and 7:150 indicts the calf-takers with a-'ajiltum amra rabbikum — the calf is the artifact of not waiting out the forty appointed nights (2:51).
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: ROOT residue = temporal displacement before a due measure. FORM adds: II = causative "make arrive early for someone" (10:11, 17:18, 18:58, 38:16, 48:20); IV = "impel to be ahead" (20:83); V = "opt for the earlier of two sanctioned points" (2:203, contrasted in-verse with ta'akhkhara); X = "seek/demand early arrival" (all 19 target God's decree); base V = "act ahead of completion"; ADJ 'ajul = characterological disposition (17:11); nominalizations = "the early-arriving one" (al-'ajilah), "the stuff of prematurity" ('ajal), and "the pre-term bovine" ('ijl). CONTEXT (punishment, revelation pace, pilgrimage days, hospitality, idol) supplies WHAT is early and WHOSE term is violated; the censure or approval (2:203 permits ta'ajjul; 48:20 is a divine favor) comes from context, not the root — the root itself is evaluatively neutral prematurity.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: 'ijl "calf" (esp. 11:69, 51:26 where it is simply food offered to guests): the lexeme could be a semantically opaque animal name (a homonym or borrowing) with no live temporal content. It is reconciled as "the not-yet-mature bovine" plus the packet-internal coupling of the calf narrative to root-haste verbs (20:83-88, 7:150, 2:51's forty nights; even 11:69 is framed by fa-ma labitha and 51:26 by faragha), but the temporal residue in the bare noun is plausible rather than independently demonstrable from verse text alone.
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: Generic "speed/quickness of motion" (velocity). Rejected as the core: the occurrences systematically measure against an appointed term, not against slowness — explicit contrast with ajal (10:11, 29:53), maw'id (18:58), ta'akhkhara (2:203), and repeated qabla-phrases (13:6, 27:46, 38:16, 20:114). 16:1 is decisive: "God's command HAS come, so do not sta'jil it" — one cannot 'speed' what has come, but one can improperly advance its moment. Velocity is what s-r-' covers; '-j-l is term-relative anticipation.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Distinct from s-r-' (rapidity of execution, no term violated), f-r-T (exceeding/letting slip), s-b-q (outstripping a co-mover in space/rank), and b-g-t (suddenness from the experiencer's side, cf. 29:53 where baghtatan and yasta'jilunaka co-occur as different things: they demand it early, it will strike them unawares). Falsifiable prediction borne out in-packet: '-j-l tokens should co-occur with term-vocabulary (ajal, maw'id, qabla, 'add/counting, ta'akhkhur) — they do in at least 12 of 47 verses — and Form X should never mean simple physical running; it never does.
unresolved_cases: 'ijl calf cluster (2:51, 2:54, 2:92, 2:93, 4:153, 7:148, 7:152, 20:88, 11:69, 51:26): reconciled (pre-mature bovine + Quran's own welding of the calf episode to a'jalaka/'ajiltu/a-'ajiltum and the forty-night term), no occurrence contradicts the residue, but the residue inside the bare noun is not independently demonstrable from internal evidence alone — this caps result strength at MODERATE rather than STRONG.
internal_discovery.rationale: 37 of 47 occurrences (all verbal forms, the adjective, and the 'ajilah/'ajal nominals) demonstrably carry "arrival/action before the due term," with the violated term named in-verse in a dozen cases — this is strong, falsifiable, and distinctive against speed-roots. The 10 calf tokens are fully reconcilable and are thematically fused to the root's haste-verbs by the text itself (20:83-88, 7:150, 2:51), so universal presence is not broken; but because their reconciliation leans on nominalization ("pre-term bovine") that the verses never assert directly, honesty requires MODERATE rather than STRONG. No occurrence is inconsistent; none forced.

adversarial_verification.notes: The packet contains two textually distinct senses. (A) A HASTE cluster of 37 occurrences (V(X) استعجل x19, V(II) عَجَّل, N(X) استعجال, V عَجَل, V(IV) أعجل, V(V) تعجّل, ADJ عَجُول, N عَجَل/العاجلة) where the proposed contribution 'forward displacement in time relative to a due term' is demonstrably present and even lexically confirmed by the تعجّل/تأخّر antonymy in 2:203 (فمن تعجّل ... ومن تأخّر) and by phrases like قبل يوم الحساب (38:16), من قبل أن يُقضى (20:114), قبل الحسنة (13:6, 27:46). (B) A CALF cluster of 10 occurrences of the noun عِجْل denoting a young bovine / the golden-calf idol: 11:69 and 51:26 (calf served to Abraham's guests), 20:88 and 7:148 (عِجْلًا جَسَدًا), and 2:51/2:54/2:92/2:93/4:153/7:152 (ٱلْعِجْلَ taken as deity). In these, 'arrival of something before its appointed/completed measure' is NOT demonstrably present in the verse text — عِجْل functions purely as an animal/object. Reconciling them would require importing an external etymology (calf = swift/young one), which the hard rules exclude as evidence. Under non-negotiable root unity, these 10 unreconciled confirmed occurrences mean universal presence does not hold. The contribution is distinctive vs nearest roots (>jl, t-A-x-r) and falsifiable for cluster A, but the polysemous calf sense refutes universal presence across the full set. Verdict: REFUTED.

occurrence_dispositions.note: Literal roasted calf (bi-ʿijlin ḥanīdh) served by Abraham to his guests. No idolatry, no violated term, no haste-verb welding — the hospitality context gives zero reinforcement. The contribution can attach only via the contested derivation 'calf = premature/not-yet-complete bovine.' Since 'ijl is an inherited Common-Semitic noun (Heb. 'ēgel, Aram. 'eglā) that may be a homonym collapsed onto ع-ج-ل rather than derived from it, the assignment rests on an unresolvable derivational question. Does not contradict the contribution (young bovine plausibly = the 'before-full-term' one) but cannot be confirmed.
Basmala is prepended in verse_text for display, but token position 5 correctly resolves to تستعجلوه in the actual verse; no tokenization artifact. Form X 'do not seek to hasten it' — CONSISTENT.

Samiri's idol-calf, but the passage welds it to the haste-field: 20:86 'afaṭāla ʿalaykumu al-ʿahd' (did the term/covenant seem too long?) and 20:83-84 Moses's own a'jalaka/'ajiltu haste verbs frame the very episode. The calf is textually re-motivated as the product of impatience against an appointed interval; the contribution attaches independent of the etymology question.

Idol-calf. The violated term is explicit in the same verse: 'We appointed Moses forty nights, THEN you took the calf during it (min ba'dih).' The calf is the artifact of not waiting out the appointed measure = forward displacement before the term's completion. Contribution holds by direct contextual anchor, not by the disputed etymology; strongest case in the set.

Moses's speech recapping 'bi-ttikhādhikumu al-'ijl' — the same forty-nights calf-taking of 2:51. The prematurity frame (sin committed during the unfinished appointed term, Moses absent) carries over; the contribution holds via the shared narrative anchor rather than the lexeme in isolation.

'thumma-ttakhadhtumu al-'ijl min baʿdih' — calf taken 'after him,' i.e., in Moses's absence before his return at the term's completion. Same idol-calf motif governed by the forty-nights frame of 2:51; forward-displacement-against-term reading holds contextually.

'ushribū fī qulūbihimu al-'ijl bi-kufrihim' — the calf-love drunk into their hearts. Same idol-calf sin of the Sinai interval; part of the coherent Quranic treatment of the calf as the artifact of not waiting out the appointed nights. No contradiction of the contribution; holds via the motif.

'ittakhadhū al-'ijl min baʿdi mā jā'athumu al-bayyināt' — same idol-calf, made after clear signs and in Moses's absence. The 'after/in the interval' framing places it in the unfinished term; the prematurity contribution attaches through the established calf narrative.

Literal fat calf (bi-ʿijlin samīn) in the same Abraham hospitality scene as 11:69. Purely zoological denotation with no thematic prematurity in context; the only bridge to the contribution is the disputed 'young = premature bovine' etymology, exposed to the same homonymy/root-collapse doubt. Not RESISTANT (no contradiction) but not cleanly CONSISTENT — genuine structural uncertainty.

'ittakhadha qawmu Mūsā min baʿdihi ... 'ijlan jasadan lahu khuwār' — idol-calf in Moses's absence, and two verses on 7:150 indicts it explicitly with the haste verb 'a-ʿajiltum amra rabbikum' (did you rush your Lord's affair?). The text itself puns the calf against haste-against-a-term; contribution holds strongly.

'alladhīna-ttakhadhū al-'ijl' — the calf-takers, directly governed by the preceding 7:150 'a-ʿajiltum amra rabbikum.' Same idol-calf welded by the Quran to the root's haste-field; forward-displacement-before-term reading is textually supported.
